sentence: The router keeps a deployment list [RDEPLOY-023].
A deployment is one way to reach an AI model: a provider, a model and the keys to call it [RDEPLOY-001], [RDEPLOY-097].
Several deployments can share one public name, called a model group [RDEPLOY-163].
When the router starts with a list, it checks each deployment and settles its deployment id [RDEPLOY-012], [RDEPLOY-007].
The same settings give the same id after a restart, unless a row lists an id with no value [RDEPLOY-007], [RDEPLOY-008].
That id ties the deployment to its own prices and its deployment budget [RDEPLOY-080], [RDEPLOY-091].
A model group's prices come from its deployments in this list [RDEPLOY-133], [RDEPLOY-138].
note: [RDEPLOY-133]: a group's members are 'The deployments named exactly the group, plus routing-group member rows of that name', or 'the wildcard deployments matching the name', all rows of `model_list`. [RDEPLOY-138]: '`input_cost_per_token` and `output_cost_per_token` take the maximum across members'. So the group's prices are derived from its deployments in the list, as stated.

sentence: One bad entry makes startup fail with that entry's error [RDEPLOY-033].
With skipping turned on, the router logs the error and leaves that entry out [RDEPLOY-033].
A failed edit can take a working model offline [RDEPLOY-209].
The model-list load builds each row in a fixed order, and the first failure ends that row's build [RDEPLOY-015]-[RDEPLOY-024].
A row with no declared id gets a SHA-256 hash of its name and expanded parameters [RDEPLOY-007].
The router appends each passing row to `model_list` and indexes it by id, by name and, when it has both a team and a team public name, by team [RDEPLOY-057].
note: [RDEPLOY-057]: appending maps the id, 'appends the position under `model_name`' and, 'When both `team_id` and `team_public_model_name` are truthy', appends it under `(team_id, team_public_model_name)` (router.py:10933 `if team_id and team_public_model_name`). The repaired sentence now carries the both-values condition. A row with an empty name is not name-indexed ([RDEPLOY-181]), but a row without a name has nothing to index by, so 'by name' does not overreach.

sentence: Runtime add and upsert run only the provider and strategy-router checks [RDEPLOY-182].

Each deployment with an id registers its model info in the process-wide catalog under that id, without prices for a strategy router, plus a filtered copy under each shared backend key [RDEPLOY-080]-[RDEPLOY-082].
deployment: one way to reach a model: a public name, provider settings with credentials, and descriptive info that carries an id (`model_name`, `litellm_params`, `model_info`)
model group: the public name callers ask for; several deployments can share it (`model_name`)
deployment id: the key of one deployment; on load, a hash of its settings when the row declares none (`model_info.id`, `generate_model_id`)
deployment list: the router's stored deployments in insertion order (`model_list`)
model-list load: the startup path that empties the registry and builds every row from the settings (`set_model_list`)
secret reference: a setting value that names an environment variable to read instead (`os.environ/`)
skip-invalid setting: a router setting: drop a bad deployment and carry on instead of failing (`ignore_invalid_deployments`)
config row: a row that came from the settings file rather than the database (`db_model`)

reserved capacity: capacity paid as a flat cost rather than per token, known as provisioned throughput (PTU); its id and price rules apply to config rows (`ptu_shares`, `LITELLM_ENABLE_PTU_COST_ATTRIBUTION`)
note: Wording changed only in how the acronym is introduced. [RDEPLOY-005]: with attribution disabled 'no flat cost accrues and this traffic is billed per token', and the warning names config-sourced rows; [RDEPLOY-015]: the PTU identity rule applies 'For a config-sourced row'. The definition is unchanged in substance and still supported.

sentence: access window: a daily interval when a deployment is reserved for the teams it lists (`access_windows`)
note: Now cites the deployment-limits claims. [LIMITS-003]: a window has `start` and `end` '(time of day)', a `timezone` and `team_ids`; [LIMITS-004]: activity 'compares only the resulting local wall-clock time of day (date is ignored)', so a daily interval; [LIMITS-008]: a deployment is dropped 'when at least one of its windows is active at `now` and `request_team_id` is `None` or is not listed in the `team_ids` of any active window', i.e. reserved for the listed teams. [RDEPLOY-016] covers the load-time validation of the setting.

sentence: environment gate: the check that keeps a row only in the environments it lists (`supported_environments`, `LITELLM_ENVIRONMENT`)
tag pattern: a regular expression a deployment declares for tag-based routing (`tag_regex`)
wildcard router: the matcher for deployments whose name holds a star (`pattern_router`)
strategy router: a deployment whose model setting marks it as a complexity, adaptive, quality or semantic router; it is not a model the router can call (`auto_router/`)
note: The unconditional 'chooses which model a request goes to' is gone. [RDEPLOY-060]: deployments are classified by `litellm_params.model`, with `auto_router/complexity_router...`, `auto_router/adaptive_router...`, `auto_router/quality_router...` and 'any other `auto_router/...`' as a semantic auto-router. [RSELECT-015] defines a strategy marker by that classification, and [RSELECT-016]'s error says such a deployment 'is a strategy router marker (auto_router/...), which is not a callable model'.

sentence: adaptive router: a strategy router that keeps learned state; built after every other row (`adaptive_routers`)
price catalog: the process-wide table of model prices and limits that every router shares (`litellm.model_cost`)
per-token prices: what one input or output token costs (`input_cost_per_token`, `output_cost_per_token`)
price reload replay: re-writing every live deployment's catalog entries after the catalog reloads (`replay_model_cost_registrations`)
runtime add, upsert, delete: the calls that change one deployment while the router runs (`add_deployment`, `upsert_deployment`, `delete_deployment`)
deployment budget: a spending cap and period for one deployment, tracked by its id (`max_budget`, `budget_duration`)
indexes: maps from an id, a name, or a team and public name to positions in the list (`model_id_to_deployment_index_map`, `model_name_to_deployment_indices`)
team public name: the name a team-owned deployment goes by for its team (`team_public_model_name`)
paused deployment: a deployment an admin has blocked (`blocked`)
deployment lookup: fetching one stored deployment by its id, or the first one of a group name (`get_deployment`, `get_deployment_by_model_group_name`)
discovered limits: token limits the router reads from an endpoint's own model listing (`arefresh_model_info`, `/v1/models`)
model alias: another name that points at a model group (`model_group_alias`)
group info: the merged description of a model group: limits, prices and capabilities (`get_model_group_info`)
note: Same wording, now citing the merge claims. [RDEPLOY-137]: the first member seeds the group with 'every field of the member's model info'; [RDEPLOY-138]: '`max_input_tokens`, `max_output_tokens`, `input_cost_per_token` and `output_cost_per_token` take the maximum across members' and the `supports_*` flags 'become `True` if any member has `True`'. [RDEPLOY-131] covers the alias entry of `get_model_group_info`.

sentence: per-minute rate limits: tokens and requests a group may use per minute (`tpm`, `rpm`)
rate-limit headers: response headers that tell the caller how much of this minute's limit is left (`x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens`)
reasoning-effort levels: the named reasoning-effort settings a group's models accept, which clients can see (`supported_reasoning_efforts`)
pin: a remembered choice that keeps related requests on one deployment for a set time (`deployment_affinity_ttl_seconds`)
When a row fails a check and `ignore_invalid_deployments` is off, the error propagates and router construction fails.
When a row fails a check and `ignore_invalid_deployments` is on, the load logs and drops the row; it retries only an unresolvable provider, at the next price reload.
When the environment settings are valid and a row's `supported_environments` lacks the current `LITELLM_ENVIRONMENT`, the load skips it with a warning, after its price entries went into the catalog.
note: The condition now carries the validity premise. [RDEPLOY-014] step 6: once the checks of steps 2-5 pass, 'the deployment is active exactly when `LITELLM_ENVIRONMENT` is in the list'; [RDEPLOY-021]: an inactive row 'is skipped. The method returns `None` and logs a warning'; [RDEPLOY-020]: pricing registration happens 'before the environment gate', so an environment-inactive row 'still leaves cost-map entries until the next replay'. Matches the figure step env>skipped.

sentence: When a config row has reserved-capacity terms while attribution is on, the load stores its per-token prices as `0.0`.
When two rows share an id and neither has reserved-capacity terms, the list keeps both; id lookups see only the later one.
When an upsert drops `max_budget` or `budget_duration`, the deployment leaves the budget limiter.
When a caller with no team asks for a group whose deployments all belong to teams, service tiers come from all its unpaused deployments, and the upstream model from the first of them.
note: Scope now matches [RDEPLOY-117] step 2: 'If none is usable, keep all of them; for a caller without a team this means every deployment when teams own all of them', then step 3 drops `blocked is True` rows. Code agrees: `_routable_deployments` uses `usable or named` after `get_all_deployments`, which for `team_id=None` keeps every row of the name ([RDEPLOY-162]). [RDEPLOY-118] returns each routable deployment's `service_tiers`; [RDEPLOY-119] returns `litellm_params.model` 'of the first routable deployment'.

sentence: When a configured token limit is present but malformed, such as `"128,000"`, the per-name lookup reports no limit when it is the first deployment's, and the group listing leaves that deployment out of the maximum.
When a deployment is deleted, its catalog entries stay until the next price reload.

When selection runs synchronously, or the async entry point runs under a router-wide routing strategy outside the five async-capable ones, no pre-routing step runs, so no strategy router chooses the model.
note: New At a glance row added next to the strategy-router fix. [RSELECT-060]: when the router-level `routing_strategy` is not one of `usage-based-routing-v2`, `simple-shuffle`, `cost-based-routing`, `latency-based-routing`, `least-busy`, 'the async entry point delegates to the synchronous selection path ... and runs no pre-routing hook'; [RSELECT-128]: 'sync selection does not run: the pre-routing hook'. Strategy routers act only through that hook ([RSELECT-105]), so none chooses the model. The pass-through entry point always runs the hook ([RSELECT-130]), but the row names 'the async entry point' specifically, so it is not contradicted.

sentence: When the router starts with a list, the model-list load builds each deployment one at a time [RDEPLOY-012], [RDEPLOY-001].
It fills in secret references and settles the deployment id, then runs a fixed series of checks [RDEPLOY-006], [RDEPLOY-007].
A failed check drops the row when the skip-invalid setting is on, and stops startup when it is off [RDEPLOY-033].
`set_model_list` empties the deployment list, its indexes and the semantic, complexity and quality registries [RDEPLOY-002].
Each top-level `os.environ/` value becomes the secret it names, except workload-identity pointer fields [RDEPLOY-006].
This pass skips nested values; registration later reads data-source endpoints and keys straight from the environment [RDEPLOY-006], [RDEPLOY-027].
A list of organizations becomes one deployment per organization, all sharing one id [RDEPLOY-009].
Nothing rolls back a failure after registration began, so a dropped row can still sit in the wildcard router [RDEPLOY-034].
Some deployments are strategy routers [RDEPLOY-060].
note: Split from the previous overstated sentence. [RDEPLOY-060] classifies deployments whose `litellm_params.model` starts with `auto_router/` as complexity, adaptive, quality or semantic strategy routers.

sentence: In the usual case, one can choose the model a request goes to, before normal selection [RSELECT-060], [RSELECT-061], [RSELECT-105].
note: Now hedged and linked to the registries. [RSELECT-061]: under one of the five async-capable router-level strategies, 'the pre-routing hook ... runs first; when it returns a response, its `model` and `messages` replace the requested ones'; [RSELECT-105]: the hook's candidates are 'gathered from those registries' (`auto_routers`, `complexity_routers`, `adaptive_routers`, `quality_routers`); [RSELECT-060] gives the exception. 'The usual case' fits the default `routing_strategy` `"simple-shuffle"` ([CFG-056]), one of the five, on the async request flow, and the new At a glance row spells out the exceptions.

sentence: The router builds most of them as each row loads [RDEPLOY-031].
It builds adaptive routers only after every row exists, so they see the whole list [RDEPLOY-011], [RDEPLOY-072].
A deployment whose model starts with `auto_router/` is a strategy router, and its prefix picks the kind: complexity, adaptive, quality or else semantic [RDEPLOY-060].
Each kind checks its own required settings, and a second router with the same name and tags is a duplicate error [RDEPLOY-061], [RDEPLOY-063], [RDEPLOY-066], [RDEPLOY-068], [RDEPLOY-069].
A complexity router that claims a licensed capability must fit under a limit the router asks for on every registration; with no limit set, there is no ceiling [RDEPLOY-065], [RDEPLOY-076].
Each deployment that has an id records its full details under that deployment id, in a price catalog that every router in the process shares [RDEPLOY-080], [RDEPLOY-188].
Those details include its per-token prices, unless it is a strategy router, which records none [RDEPLOY-082].
So two deployments of one model can carry different prices [RDEPLOY-213].
Each deployment also writes a filtered copy under each shared backend key, keeping only catalog fields and none of its own prices [RDEPLOY-081].
Before registering, a row can fill missing prices from its underlying model's built-in entry, in four steps that each need their own condition [RDEPLOY-020]:
Off-peak base rates, only when off-peak pricing is on and the row sets no input per-token price, no input per-second price, no general per-second price and no tiered pricing [RDEPLOY-028].
note: Fixed. The four blockers now match RDEPLOY-028 one for one: 'none of `input_cost_per_token`, `input_cost_per_second`, `cost_per_second` or `tiered_pricing` is set' (code router.py:9895-9898 checks exactly those, each `is not None`). 'Input per-second' and 'general per-second' no longer take in `output_cost_per_second`. 'Only when' is a necessary condition, which leaves room for the silent no-op of RDEPLOY-029. 'Off-peak base rates' is the spec's own label (RDEPLOY-020) and the function's name.

sentence: Cache prices, only when an input price is set; an explicit `0.0` counts as set [RDEPLOY-020].
Service-tier prices, skipped when neither per-token price is set [RDEPLOY-020].
note: Reworded next to the off-peak fix ('base rate' became 'per-token price'). [RDEPLOY-020]: service-tier prices are 'skipped when both `input_cost_per_token` and `output_cost_per_token` are `None`'. The further skip for PTU terms with attribution on ([RDEPLOY-035]) is an extra case that this 'skipped when' statement does not deny.

sentence: The tiered output rate, only for tiered pricing that lacks an output rate [RDEPLOY-030].
Take two deployments of openai/gpt-4o: cheap sets both per-token prices to 0.0, and std sets none [RDEPLOY-213].
Cheap's entry holds the 0.0 prices plus inherited built-in ones, such as a cache-read price of 1.25e-06 [RDEPLOY-213].
Std's entry holds only its id, while the shared gpt-4o entry keeps 2.5e-06 input and 1e-05 output, so std's deployment info reports those built-in prices [RDEPLOY-213], [RDEPLOY-130].

Every registration is non-persistent, so after a catalog reload each live router's `replay_model_cost_registrations` retries the queued provider failures, re-registers every row still in its list, and clears group caches [RDEPLOY-188], [RDEPLOY-085], [RDEPLOY-086].
Only routers built with a list take part [RDEPLOY-012].
While the router runs, the proxy can add, edit or delete one deployment at a time [RDEPLOY-040], [RDEPLOY-046], [RDEPLOY-053].
These changes skip most of the checks that loading applies [RDEPLOY-042].
An edit removes the old version before it adds the new one, so a failed edit can leave a model without its working deployment [RDEPLOY-047], [RDEPLOY-209].
`add_deployment` returns nothing when the id already exists, and a deployment built without an id gets a random one [RDEPLOY-040], [RDEPLOY-045].
It has no error handling, and it syncs the budget after storing the row, so a budget error leaves the row stored and routable [RDEPLOY-043].
`upsert_deployment` first looks up the id and strips capability fields; an error there propagates whatever the skip-invalid setting says, and nothing changes [RDEPLOY-049].
It returns nothing when name, provider settings and model info all match the stored row [RDEPLOY-046].
Otherwise it removes the old row, releases its strategy slots and adds the new one at the end of the list [RDEPLOY-047].
A failure later in the upsert ends as follows [RDEPLOY-049], [RDEPLOY-051]:
Skip-invalid on, failure before the new row is stored: the router re-adds the old deployment at the end and logs that it restored it [RDEPLOY-049], [RDEPLOY-050].
If that re-add fails too, it logs a warning and the old row stays gone; an id that was new has nothing to restore [RDEPLOY-050].
Skip-invalid on, failure after the new row is stored, as in the budget sync or the adaptive pass: the failed row stays and the old one is gone [RDEPLOY-049], [RDEPLOY-215].
Skip-invalid off: the error propagates and nothing restores the old row; a failure after the new row is stored leaves that row in place [RDEPLOY-051].
`delete_deployment` returns the removed row, or nothing for an unknown id [RDEPLOY-053].
It repairs every index, unregisters the budget and releases strategy slots [RDEPLOY-053], [RDEPLOY-058].
Apart from a failed strategy-slot release, which it logs while still returning the row, it swallows any error and returns nothing, even after the row left the list [RDEPLOY-054], [RDEPLOY-055].
note: The exception now has its referent. [RDEPLOY-054]: a failure while releasing strategy slots 'is logged at error level with traceback ... The deletion still returns the removed row'; [RDEPLOY-055]: 'Any other exception during deletion is swallowed silently and `None` is returned, even if the row was already popped.'

sentence: 0s, deployment d2: serves m on gpt-4o; state: serving m.
1 min, deployment d2: edit names an unknown provider; state: old m restored at end.
1 min, callers of model m: requests still reach m; state: served.
2 min, deployment d2: edit to adaptive router, no settings; state: stored as m3.
2 min, callers of model m: m has no deployment left; state: m gone.
The router finds deployments through three indexes: by deployment id, by name, and by team [RDEPLOY-187].
Many answers about a model name come from its first deployment in list order, and an edit moves a deployment to the end, which can change those answers [RDEPLOY-197].
The first-deployment answers are the by-name deployment lookup, configured mode, display name, token limits, upstream model and the adaptive router's cost reading [RDEPLOY-197], [RDEPLOY-070].
A team-owned deployment counts as usable only by its own team; one with no team is usable by everyone [RDEPLOY-098].
Credential lookup tries the id, the name, the team public name, then a wildcard, and returns nothing for a paused deployment [RDEPLOY-099].
Discovered limits fill only gaps: a configured limit that is present always wins [RDEPLOY-110].

`arefresh_model_info` probes only deployments whose provider resolves to `"hosted_vllm"`, `"openai"`, `"text-completion-openai"` or `"openai_like"`, that have a base address, no star in the model and no client-side credentials [RDEPLOY-106].
A probe that misses the cache sends one request to `/v1/models` with a 5-second timeout, and up to 8 probes run at a time [RDEPLOY-105], [RDEPLOY-108].
The router keeps discovered limits for 600 s and discards a result whose row was replaced during the probe [RDEPLOY-109].
To describe a model group, the router merges every deployment behind it [RDEPLOY-133], [RDEPLOY-138].
Limits and prices take the largest value, most features count when any member has them, and per-minute rate limits add up [RDEPLOY-138], [RDEPLOY-134].

`get_model_group_info` follows a model alias one hop, then gathers the deployments named exactly the group plus routing-group members of that name, or the matching wildcard deployments when there are none [RDEPLOY-131], [RDEPLOY-133].
The first member seeds the answer, and later members widen it, except in these fields [RDEPLOY-137], [RDEPLOY-138]:
Fast mode holds only when every member supports it [RDEPLOY-139].
Reasoning-effort levels are the intersection, and one unknown member makes the group unknown [RDEPLOY-140].
The supported-parameter list takes the latest member's value that is set, even an empty one [RDEPLOY-138].
note: [RDEPLOY-138]: '`supported_openai_params` is replaced by the latest non-`None` value'. 'Set, even an empty one' matches the `is not None` test, so an empty list replaces the group's list.

sentence: Client-side auth settings come from the last member, when it sets them [RDEPLOY-141].
One memo shared by every router in the process caches these answers, and any router's change clears every router's entries [RDEPLOY-143].
After a call, the router stamps the group name on the response and, when it knows the group, the rate-limit headers [RDEPLOY-147].
A rate-limit header the provider already sent keeps the provider's value, and the router still adds its other ones [RDEPLOY-148].
For example, a group with `tpm` 5000 and `rpm` 50 that used 500 tokens and 5 requests this minute reports 4500 tokens and 45 requests remaining [RDEPLOY-146].
Remaining tokens can go negative, while remaining input and output tokens stop at 0 [RDEPLOY-146].

Step prep, Fill secrets, settle the id: Each top-level secret reference in the provider settings becomes its value, except workload-identity pointer fields [RDEPLOY-006]. A row that declares no id gets one made from its settings, the same after every restart [RDEPLOY-007].

Step rules, Check capacity and windows: Every row's access window settings must be valid [RDEPLOY-016]. A config row with reserved capacity needs an id of its own, but only when flat-cost billing is on or the row splits its capacity among teams [RDEPLOY-015].

Step price, Record prices before the gate: The row's prices go into the price catalog before the environment check, so a row skipped or rejected later still leaves an entry until the next price reload [RDEPLOY-020].

Step env>skipped, Skip rows for other environments: When the environment settings are valid, a row that lists environments stays only if the current environment is one of them; otherwise the router skips it with a warning [RDEPLOY-014], [RDEPLOY-021].
Step env>failed, Bad environment settings fail: A missing or invalid current environment, or an invalid listed one, raises an error instead of skipping the row [RDEPLOY-014].
Step valid, Check patterns and provider: Every tag pattern must compile, and the provider must be one the router knows, unless the row names a prompt-management model [RDEPLOY-022], [RDEPLOY-024].
Step failed, Drop the row, or stop: With the skip-invalid setting off, the first failure stops the router from starting; with it on, the router drops the row and moves on [RDEPLOY-033].

Step stored, Store and index: A passing row joins the end of the deployment list and the lookups by id and name, and by team when it has both a team and a team public name [RDEPLOY-023], [RDEPLOY-057].
note: [RDEPLOY-023]: a passing row 'is then appended to `model_list` ... and indexed'; [RDEPLOY-057] indexes by team only 'When both `team_id` and `team_public_model_name` are truthy', which the repaired step now states.

sentence: Deployments the proxy adds or edits at runtime skip the environment, tag-pattern and access window checks, and the secret expansion, that loading applies [RDEPLOY-207]. One can serve in the wrong environment or carry an unexpanded secret reference [RDEPLOY-207].

A failed edit can take a working model offline [RDEPLOY-209], [RDEPLOY-215]. With the skip-invalid setting off, the edit fails with its error and nothing restores the old deployment [RDEPLOY-209]. With it on, a failure late in the edit keeps the broken new one, while the router's warning says it is dropping it [RDEPLOY-215].

A list of organizations on one deployment becomes several deployments sharing one deployment id [RDEPLOY-208]. A failure on one of them cools down all of them, and lookups by id find only the last one [RDEPLOY-208].
note: The admin-pause wording is gone; the sentence now follows [RDEPLOY-208]: 'An `organization` list expands to one deployment per organization, all sharing one id' and 'Impact: a failure on one organization's deployment cools down all of them, and id lookups find only the last one.'

sentence: Building any router from a list of deployments silently stops feedback to the adaptive routers of every other router in the same process [RDEPLOY-206].
One deployment whose model the price catalog does not list hides a whole group's reasoning-effort levels from clients [RDEPLOY-210].

A second router in one process can end up using the first router's pin cache and settings [RDEPLOY-216]. This happens when its strategy router pins requests with the same pin lifetime as the first router's pinning check [RDEPLOY-214].
